=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The auto-merge cancel block only fires when the gate job's evaluate step runs, which happens on every `pull_request` or `workflow_dispatch` event. The workflow has no `issue_comment` trigger, and the gate job is not invoked from any other surface. A `hold` claim posted via PR comment without a corresponding push or dispatch will not trigger the cancel, leaving an existing enrollment armed.
  WHY: An attacker (or operator) who can post a comment containing a `hold` claim — but cannot push — can race the gate against a long-pole required check. The sequence: a previous review run enrolls head A in auto-merge, the attacker posts a `hold` claim, no review run is triggered, the pending required check clears, and GitHub merges head A without re-running the merge hold gate. This reproduces the original security finding the PR claims to fix.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The cancel call uses direct `gh pr merge` (no `gh_retry`), so a single transient API failure (network, rate limit, GitHub 5xx) leaves the enrollment armed until the next push.
  WHY: A transient GitHub error during the cancel will log `result=failed` and emit a `::warning::`, but the enrollment stays armed. Until the next push (which could be hours later if the fix is the next head push by the same session), the PR can still auto-merge without the gate re-running. The `claude-pr-catch-all` sweep does not cancel enrollments, so there is no other safety net.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Both stdout and stderr are redirected to /dev/null, so when the cancel call fails, the underlying `gh` error message is discarded.
  WHY: When the cancel fails (e.g., 401 token revocation, 403 forbidden, 422 because the PR moved between read and cancel), the operator cannot tell which failure mode triggered the warning, so they cannot pick the right remediation.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The projection already normalizes `auto_merge` to a boolean, and the extraction re-evaluates the same condition with a slightly different formulation (`(.auto_merge // false)`).
  WHY: The formulations agree today, but a future change to one without the other can drift; this is a maintenance hazard rather than a runtime bug.
- README.md; agents.md; changelog.d/5565-claude-sync-merge.md | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The docs call the cancel call "1 GraphQL mutation", but `gh pr merge --disable-auto` uses the REST API.
  WHY: The inaccurate description is misleading for readers reasoning about API budgets because GraphQL and REST are tracked separately.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- review_autofix.yml:545-550; internal-review.yml:10-25 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Cancellation of an existing auto-merge enrollment only runs when a review workflow run occurs. The wrapper has no `issue_comment` trigger, so posting a `hold` claim on an already-enrolled `claude/*` PR does not invoke cancellation.
  WHY: If required checks are pending, a hold comment alone starts no run. The enrollment remains armed, and GitHub can merge the PR when checks pass without re-running the hold gate. A cancellation failure at review_autofix.yml:548-550 also leaves the enrollment armed.
  HARDENING_SUGGESTION: Preserve stderr in the workflow log while suppressing stdout.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

  WHY: For a pre-existing auto-merge enrollment, a hold claim posted without a subsequent push leaves the enrollment armed. When pending required checks clear, GitHub merges the PR without re-running the hold gate. The PR description acknowledges this in AD-4 ("no separate hold-triggered cancellation").
